title: Location Tracking via GPS
description: Continuous GPS position data collection enables precise location tracking of the user, potentially revealing sensitive locations (home, workplace, medical facilities) and movement patterns over time.
assumptions: User is aware of GPS tracking but may not realize the extent of location data collection

title: Biometric Identification via Heart Rate
description: Heart rate data can be used to identify individuals and infer health status, creating a persistent biometric identifier that could be linked to personal identity.
assumptions: Heart rate patterns are unique to individuals and can be used for identification

title: Unintended Health Data Sharing
description: Continuous health monitoring data may be shared with third parties (insurance, employers, advertisers) without user consent or awareness.
assumptions: Data sharing agreements exist between device manufacturers and third parties

title: Data Interception During Transmission
description: Sensor telemetry data transmitted from wearable device to cloud/server could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transit.
assumptions: Data transmission may not be fully encrypted or may use weak encryption

title: Location Meta-data in Transmission
description: Meta-data about the data flow (timestamps, packet sizes, routing information) could reveal when and where the user is located based on transmission patterns.
assumptions: Transmission patterns correlate with user location and activity

title: Data Disclosure to Third Parties
description: Wearable device may share collected sensor data with third parties (app developers, advertisers, service providers) without explicit user consent.
assumptions: Device manufacturer has business relationships with third-party data processors

title: Unintended Health Profile Creation
description: Continuous collection of health metrics could create detailed health profiles that are used for purposes other than the user's intended use (e.g., insurance underwriting, employment decisions).
assumptions: Health data is aggregated and analyzed to create user profiles

title: Data interception during transmission
description: Sensor data (GPS traces, device ID, timestamps) transmitted between wearable device and companion app could be intercepted by third parties, potentially exposing user location and device identity.
assumptions: Data is transmitted over network without end-to-end encryption

title: Lawful basis for data collection
description: Wearable device collects sensitive data (GPS traces, device ID) that may require explicit user consent and legal basis for processing under privacy regulations.
assumptions: User consent may not be obtained or may be insufficient for all data types collected

title: Insufficient notice of data collection
description: Users may not be adequately informed about what data is being collected and shared with the companion app, including the extent of GPS tracking and device identification.
assumptions: Privacy policy may not clearly explain data sharing practices

title: Unintended data processing
description: Companion app may process received sensor data in ways not intended by the user, such as sharing with third parties, using for profiling, or retaining data beyond necessary retention periods.
assumptions: App may have broader data usage than initially disclosed

title: Data quality issues in processing
description: Companion app may process GPS traces and timestamps incorrectly, leading to inaccurate exercise session data or incorrect location tracking.
assumptions: App may lack proper data validation or error handling

title: Unintended Disclosure of Health Data
description: User may not be aware that their calorie, meal, and weight data could be disclosed to third parties, advertisers, or other entities beyond the companion app's intended users.

title: Identification via Data Flow Meta-data
description: Meta-data about the parties (user and app) in the data flow could be used to link or identify the user, potentially revealing their identity or associations with the companion app.

title: Unintended Use of Health Data
description: The companion app may use the user's health data for purposes beyond the intended scope, such as targeted advertising, research, or sharing with third parties without explicit consent.

title: Inappropriate User Identification
description: The mobile app may collect and transmit more identifying information than necessary for the health logging functionality, potentially including device identifiers, location data, or other personal information beyond the health logs themselves.
assumptions: Assumes the app collects minimal required data for health logging functionality

title: Unauthorized Data Disclosure
description: The mobile app may disclose health log data to third parties (e.g., advertisers, data brokers, or other services) without explicit user consent or appropriate privacy controls.
assumptions: Assumes the app has mechanisms to share data with third parties

title: Data Flow Identification
description: Meta-data about the data flow (e.g., timing, frequency, volume, and content patterns) could be used to link users or identify individuals based on their health logging behavior.
assumptions: Assumes data flows are observable and potentially analyzable

title: Health Data Disclosure
description: The health log store may disclose sensitive health information to unauthorized parties through inadequate access controls, data breaches, or improper sharing mechanisms.
assumptions: Assumes the data store has access control mechanisms that may be compromised

title: Health Data Unavailability
description: The health log store may make health data unavailable to users due to technical failures, service interruptions, or intentional data deletion without proper user notification or recovery mechanisms.
assumptions: Assumes the data store has availability mechanisms that may fail

title: Unintended Location Tracking
description: The mobile app collects and shares GPS location traces with timestamps, enabling continuous tracking of user movements and behavior patterns.
assumptions: Assumes the app has access to GPS hardware and can transmit location data.

title: User Identification via Location Data
description: Location traces with timestamps can be used to identify and track specific individuals, potentially revealing personal habits, routines, and sensitive locations.
assumptions: Assumes location data is unique enough to identify individuals.

title: Location Data Interception in Transit
description: GPS location traces transmitted from the mobile app to the location history store could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during data transmission.
assumptions: Assumes data is transmitted over a network that may not be fully secured.

title: Persistent Location History Storage
description: The location history store retains GPS traces indefinitely, enabling long-term tracking of user movements and creating a comprehensive movement profile.
assumptions: Assumes the store retains data without proper retention policies.

title: Unauthorized Access to Stored Location Data
description: Location history stored in DS2 could be accessed by unauthorized parties, potentially revealing sensitive personal information about user movements and habits.
assumptions: Assumes the store has appropriate access controls.

title: Non-compliance with Location Privacy Regulations
description: The location history store may not comply with applicable privacy regulations regarding location data collection, storage, and sharing.
assumptions: Assumes the store operates in a jurisdiction with location privacy regulations.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain - depends on specific jurisdiction and compliance framework.

title: Health Data Linkage Across Sessions
description: The Health Log Store shares calorie, weight, and exercise logs across multiple sessions, enabling linkage of data points about the same individual over time, which could be used to build comprehensive health profiles.
assumptions: Assumes logs are not properly anonymized and session identifiers are not sufficiently protected.

title: Health Condition Inference
description: The source element shares detailed health metrics (calorie, weight, exercise) that could be used to infer sensitive health conditions or medical history, even if not explicitly disclosed.
assumptions: Assumes the analytics service may use these data points to derive health conclusions.

title: Health Profile Construction
description: The Health Analytics Service processes and combines health logs across sessions to construct comprehensive health profiles, which could be used to identify individuals and their health status.
assumptions: Assumes the analytics service aggregates data without adequate anonymization.

title: Sensitive Health Information Disclosure
description: The analytics service may process health data in ways that reveal sensitive health conditions or medical information, potentially exceeding the original data collection purpose.
assumptions: Assumes the analytics service may use data for purposes beyond the original health-condition analysis intent.

title: Data Flow Linkage Metadata
description: The data flow itself may contain metadata about the parties involved (e.g., session identifiers, timestamps, data patterns) that could be used to link or identify individuals across different data sources.
assumptions: Assumes metadata about the data flow is not adequately protected or anonymized.

title: Location data sharing without consent
description: Location history data is shared from the data store to analytics service without explicit user consent, potentially violating privacy expectations around location tracking.
assumptions: Users may not be aware their location history is being accessed for analytics purposes.

title: Location data enables individual identification
description: Location history data can be used to identify and track specific individuals, potentially revealing sensitive personal information about their movements and habits.
assumptions: Location patterns are unique enough to identify individuals.

title: Location data interception during transmission
description: Location history data in transit between data store and analytics service could be intercepted by unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Data transmission may not be adequately encrypted or protected.

title: Location pattern analysis reveals sensitive information
description: The analytics service derives daily routine and movement patterns from location data, which could reveal sensitive information about user habits, health status, or personal activities.
assumptions: Movement patterns can be correlated with sensitive personal information.

title: Analytics service identifies individuals from location patterns
description: The health analytics service may use location pattern analysis to identify and profile specific individuals, potentially creating detailed personal profiles.
assumptions: Location patterns are distinctive enough for individual identification.

title: Location analytics data disclosed to unauthorized parties
description: Processed location analytics data could be disclosed to unauthorized third parties or used for purposes beyond the original intent.
assumptions: Data sharing controls may not be adequate.

title: Insufficient legal basis for data sharing
description: The Health Analytics Service may share inferred health insights without a clear legal basis or adequate consent from users, potentially violating data protection requirements.
assumptions: Assumes the service operates under general data protection frameworks

title: Inaccurate or misleading health insights
description: The inferred health-condition risk indicators, routine summaries, and trend flags may be inaccurate or misleading, potentially causing users to make incorrect health decisions.
assumptions: Assumes the analytics algorithm may have limitations or errors

title: Insufficient notification of data sharing
description: Users may not be adequately notified about the specific health insights being shared with the Companion Mobile App and the implications of this sharing.
assumptions: Assumes notification practices may be incomplete or unclear

title: Data flow metadata exposure
description: Meta-data about the parties being used to link or identify them may be exposed during data transmission, potentially allowing correlation of health insights with user identities.
assumptions: Assumes data flow metadata may contain identifying information

title: Unauthorized disclosure of health insights
description: The Companion Mobile App may disclose the received health insights to third parties without proper authorization or user consent.
assumptions: Assumes the app may have inadequate access controls

title: Unintended use of health insights
description: The Companion Mobile App may use the health insights in ways not intended by the user or the Health Analytics Service, potentially leading to privacy concerns.
assumptions: Assumes the app may have broader data usage capabilities than intended

title: Unauthorized Access to Health Data at Cloud Provider
description: The third-party cloud hosting provider may have unauthorized access to the sensitive health and location data, models, and analytics data stored on their infrastructure, potentially leading to data breaches and privacy violations.
assumptions: Assumes the cloud provider has appropriate security controls in place, but third-party access risks remain.

title: Data Loss at Cloud Provider
description: The cloud hosting provider may experience data loss due to technical failures, natural disasters, or other incidents affecting their infrastructure, resulting in loss of the health and location datasets.
assumptions: Assumes the cloud provider has appropriate disaster recovery and backup mechanisms.

title: Data Interception During Transit
description: The analytics data, models, and health/location datasets may be intercepted during transmission from the Health Analytics Service to the Cloud Hosting Provider, potentially exposing sensitive information.
assumptions: Assumes data is transmitted over networks that may not be fully secured.

title: Loss of Confidentiality at Source
description: The Health Analytics Service may share sensitive health and location data with the third-party cloud provider without adequate confidentiality protections, potentially leading to unauthorized disclosure.
assumptions: Assumes the sharing decision was made without full consideration of privacy implications.
